facts.fact: The National Bank of Ethiopia issued Directive ONPS/10/2025, in force 12 May 2025, amending its directive on licensing and authorization of payment instrument issuers, setting capital, ownership and conduct requirements for licensed issuers.
facts.system: Licensing and Authorization of Payment Instrument Issuer Directive ONPS/09/2023 as amended by ONPS/10/2025

ETH.note: Directive sets security and limit rules; no consumer-protection or conduct rules for digital finance are stated beyond a recital.
Only an exemption mentioning inward remittances from a daily limit; no corridor stated.
Nothing on government payments to people.
Nothing on the national ID system.
Real-time KYC validation is required but no check against the national ID is stated.

facts.fact: National Bank of Ethiopia Directive ONPS/10/2025, issued under National Payment Systems Proclamation 718 as amended, entered into force on 12 May 2025.
The directive sets licensing, capital (Birr 100 million) and shareholding rules for payment instrument issuers, allowing telecom operators among the permitted large shareholders.

The directive requires payment instrument issuers to interoperate wallet-to-wallet through the national switch or another licensed switch operator, and all financial institutions providing digital financial services to participate in the national switch's instant payment system; in force 12 May 2025.

The National Bank of Ethiopia's directive of 12 May 2025 sets limits on Level 2 electronic money accounts, person-to-person transfers (Birr 75,000 daily) and QR merchant payments (Birr 250,000 daily), and sets a deadline for existing licensed issuers to raise capital.
